activity_statements.statement: designs and sells GPU chips and accelerated computing systems for AI training and inference in data centers for cloud providers, enterprises, and governments
develops and licenses the CUDA software platform and AI developer SDKs enabling researchers and engineers to build AI applications on NVIDIA hardware
builds and sells RTX graphics processing units for consumer gaming and professional visualization markets with AI-powered ray tracing and DLSS rendering
operates the Omniverse industrial digitalization platform enabling digital twin creation and simulation for manufacturing, automotive, and engineering firms
provides NVIDIA DRIVE platform (chips, software, simulation) for autonomous vehicle perception and decision-making to automotive OEMs
offers AI-powered computing infrastructure (DGX systems, HGX server boards) for healthcare institutions running medical imaging, genomics, and clinical AI workloads
builds networking hardware (InfiniBand, Ethernet switches via Mellanox acquisition) for high-bandwidth AI cluster interconnects in data centers

name_reality_gap: Index labels it as 'Computer Hardware Manufacturing' but NVIDIA is now primarily an AI infrastructure and software platform company — the majority of its extraordinary revenue growth comes from AI data center workloads, not traditional PC graphics cards. The hardware is the substrate; the ecosystem of CUDA software and developer tools is the moat.
extraction_notes: Investor annual report page timed out. Product and about pages gave solid coverage. Segment revenue weighting estimated based on public knowledge of NVIDIA's FY2025 results where Data Center exceeded 85% of revenue.
